answer_text:
Let

\[
A_k=\operatorname{arccot}(k(k-1)),\qquad k\ge 1,
\]

with the convention \(\operatorname{arccot}(0)=\frac{\pi}{2}\). We will show that the \(k\)-th term of the series telescopes as

\[
\operatorname{arccot}\frac{1-k^2+k^4}{2k}=A_k-A_{k+1}.
\]

Set

\[
x=k(k-1),\qquad y=k(k+1).
\]

Then \(0\le x<y\), so \(0<A_k-A_{k+1}<\frac{\pi}{2}\). Using the identity

\[
\cot(u-v)=\frac{\cot u\cot v+1}{\cot v-\cot u},
\]

we get

\[
\cot(A_k-A_{k+1})
=
\frac{xy+1}{y-x}.
\]

Now

\[
xy=k(k-1)\cdot k(k+1)=k^4-k^2,
\]

and

\[
y-x=k(k+1)-k(k-1)=2k.
\]

Therefore

\[
\cot(A_k-A_{k+1})
=
\frac{k^4-k^2+1}{2k}.
\]

Since \(0<A_k-A_{k+1}<\frac{\pi}{2}\), this implies

\[
A_k-A_{k+1}
=
\operatorname{arccot}\frac{k^4-k^2+1}{2k}
=
\operatorname{arccot}\frac{1-k^2+k^4}{2k}.
\]

Thus the partial sum is telescoping:

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{N}\operatorname{arccot}\frac{1-k^2+k^4}{2k}
=
\sum_{k=1}^{N}(A_k-A_{k+1})
=
A_1-A_{N+1}.
\]

Now

\[
A_1=\operatorname{arccot}(0)=\frac{\pi}{2},
\]

and

\[
A_{N+1}=\operatorname{arccot}(N(N+1)).
\]

Hence

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{N}\operatorname{arccot}\frac{1-k^2+k^4}{2k}
=
\frac{\pi}{2}-\operatorname{arccot}(N(N+1)).
\]

Taking \(N\to\infty\), since \(\operatorname{arccot}(N(N+1))\to 0\),

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\operatorname{arccot}\frac{1-k^2+k^4}{2k}
=
\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]

\[
\boxed{\frac{\pi}{2}}
\]
